root_causes.description: product-catalog is the sole shared downstream of the three services displaying the 10s p99 spike (frontend, checkout, recommendation) and is the only component with a resource anomaly (CPU ~1.93 cores, ~100x its peers). Its degraded request handling inflates the server-span p99 of every caller to the 10s ceiling, surfacing as high latency at the user-facing frontend.

evidence.observed_value: mean=2.291, p99=4.353, max=4.370 ms (cart is a leaf, not behind product-catalog -> unaffected)
mean=2.661, p99=4.940, max=4.940 ms (ad is a leaf -> unaffected)

root_causes.description: Alternative reading: the ~1.93-core CPU burn at product-catalog (vs ~0.01 cores for peers) is a classic CPU-stress injection signature; CPU starvation then makes product-catalog slow, producing the 10s p99 seen at all of its callers. Same root service, different injected-mechanism label.

evidence.observed_value: mean=1.934 cores, max=2.240 cores (~100x peer services)
mean=0.015 cores (normal; frontend is not CPU-bound)
p99=10000 ms (latency consequence of product-catalog CPU starvation)

root_causes.description: If the incident label names the alerting/symptom service rather than the injection target, frontend itself exhibits the latency spike (p99=10s) that generated the alert. This is the user-visible surface, but topology shows frontend is an upstream caller, not the origin of the delay.

evidence.observed_value: mean=0.015 cores (frontend is NOT resource-saturated; argues against a frontend-local fault)

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog pods for injected stress/chaos (CPU throttling, StressChaos) and remove the fault once identified (kubectl top pod -n otel-demo; describe pod for chaos annotations).

Check product-catalog resource limits/requests and CPU throttling; raise CPU limit or scale replicas if the saturation is organic, since catalog is the shared hot path for frontend, checkout and recommendation.
If latency is injected rather than CPU-bound, remove the latency injection on the product-catalog service/pod network path.
Add caching / reduce per-request catalog work in product-catalog to lower its baseline CPU.
Validate recovery by confirming frontend, checkout and recommendation p99 latencies return below ~10 ms and product-catalog CPU returns to ~0.02 cores.
